title: Lean Derivation Redraft With Negatives

canonical_node.axiom: A derivation chain must prove both what the framework affirms and what it excludes, including failures under missing conditions and apparent coherence under pressure.
definitions: Positive derivation lane: constructive proofs of what the framework defines, proves, maps, and names.
Negative derivation lane: proofs of what cannot reverse, cannot self-repair, collapses under zero factor, is insufficient, invalid bridge forms, and coercive or false-positive patterns fail.
Adversarial lane: records critic objections, rival explanations, and formal responses, including what Lean does not prove.
Bridge/coverage ledger: ties lanes together, showing which claims have negative/adversarial tests and which modules remain one-sided.
derivation: The current derivation chain only walks the constructive chain, leaving negative and adversarial value untapped.
A full test architecture requires at least five to ten negative or adversarial derivation families attached to the same structure.
The redraft organizes into three lanes plus a bridge ledger: positive, negative, adversarial, and coverage ledger.

The negative lane includes families: zero-factor sufficiency failures, non-reversal, insufficiency, counterfeit coherence, bridge invalidation, moral asymmetry, memory/scar persistence, mediation necessity, dependency lattice impossibility, adversarial false-victory.

The redrafted run order: foundations, stage/transition, mapping/bridge, field controls/invariance, score/dependency lattice, polarity/fracture, persistence/conversion, mediation/justice/mission, chi evaluation, negative lane, adversarial lane.
Public-status vocabulary ensures honest claims: LEAN_PROVEN, REJECTION_PROVEN, STRUCTURALLY_MAPPED, THEOLOGICALLY_IDENTIFIED, ADVERSARIAL_TESTED, NOT_YET_FORMALIZED.
canonical_node.action: Redraft the Lean workbook into at least four tabs: LEAN_POSITIVE_CHAIN, LEAN_NEGATIVE_CHAIN, LEAN_ADVERSARIAL_CHAIN, LEAN_COVERAGE_LEDGER, and run the full derivation in the specified order.
boundary: Does not itself provide formal proofs; it is a plan for organizing derivations.
Does not claim that any specific negative theorem has been proven in Lean.
Does not define the exact content of each derivation family beyond examples.
test: Check that the workbook contains at least five to ten negative derivation families.
Check that each positive claim has corresponding negative and adversarial tests where applicable.
Check that the coverage ledger identifies modules with missing rejection coverage.
Check that public-status tags are applied consistently to every line.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Adds a structured plan for negative and adversarial derivation families, enabling a full test architecture that proves exclusions and failure conditions.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the existing positive derivation chain and its constructive proofs.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this redraft, the derivation run remains one-sided, lacking negative and adversarial tests, reducing trustworthiness and leaving overclaims unguarded.

overstatement_risks: May be mistaken for a claim that negative theorems are already proven.
May be mistaken for a formal specification of the derivation families.
May be mistaken for a guarantee that the redraft will produce trustworthy results.
kill_conditions: If the redraft is presented as having already produced negative proofs.
If the plan is treated as a substitute for actual formalization.
If the public-status tags are used to claim more than is proven.
risk.lean_target: Formalize at least one negative derivation family (e.g., zero-factor sufficiency failure) in Lean.

plain_summary: This document is a plan to redraft the Lean derivation workbook to include negative and adversarial derivation families, ensuring the framework proves not only what it affirms but also what it excludes. It outlines three lanes (positive, negative, adversarial) plus a coverage ledger, and specifies ten negative derivation families to add. It does not itself provide formal proofs.
